main_diagnosis: The simulator is missing a slow K+ M-current (IM) channel responsible for spike-frequency adaptation. With only fast Na+/K+ and leak channels, the model cannot reproduce the subthreshold dynamics and firing rate adaptation seen in experimental recordings. The high neg_avg_log_marginal_NLE (26.6) strongly suggests a systematic mismatch in spike-rate adaptation or subthreshold resonance that a single additional gating variable can fix. The editable sections under tau_V_inv and V_inf in the simulation loop, plus the kinetics section, are the key locations that need modification.

issues.description: Missing slow K+ M-current (IM) channel: without it the model cannot reproduce spike-frequency adaptation. gbar_X1 (range [1e-4, 10] mS/cm²) should be used as the M-current conductance, reusing E_K = -107 mV so no extra reversal potential parameter is needed. param_j (negated, raw range [1e-4, 3000]) can serve as a slow time-constant numerator (e.g. tau_max ≈ hundreds of ms), and param_i can serve as a voltage offset or half-activation parameter (negated, raw range [1e-4, 150]).
issues.location: All four EDITABLE SECTIONs: kinetics definitions, state-variable declarations, initialization, and the simulation loop (tau_V_inv / V_inf / state update).

issues.description: gbar_X2 and its channel are unused: if the M-current alone does not fully close the gap, a second channel (e.g. T-type Ca²⁺ current with E_Ca ≈ param_i interpreted as a positive reversal) could be added, but only after verifying M-current alone is insufficient, to respect the 'keep the model as simple as possible' directive.
issues.location: params[:, 7] extraction and all four EDITABLE SECTIONs.
issues.suggestion: Leave gbar_X2 extracted but unused for now. If post-M-current metrics remain high (neg_avg_log_marginal_NLE >> 10), add a T-type Ca²⁺ channel using gbar_X2 with two gating variables (m_T, h_T) and E_Ca = |param_i| as a positive reversal potential, following standard Destexhe/Huguenard T-channel kinetics.
